product_one_liner.value: Fly.io is a public cloud for developers to deploy and run applications, databases and AI agents on hardware-isolated Linux virtual machines.
product_one_liner.notes: The homepage describes the public cloud and isolation model; the company profile explains developer deployment of apps and databases; Sprites documentation establishes AI-agent workloads. Sources: https://fly.io/, https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/fly-io and https://docs.fly.io/sprites.

pricing_page.notes: Fly.io has a public pricing page: https://fly.io/pricing.

named_customers.notes: named_customers: The homepage attributes customer testimonials to Mocha and Steel.dev and links their customer stories. Sources: https://fly.io/, https://fly.io/customer-stories/mocha/ and https://fly.io/customer-stories/steel-dev/. | named_customers.0: The homepage customer testimonial names Mocha and links its customer story: https://fly.io/customer-stories/mocha/. | named_customers.1: The homepage customer testimonial names Steel.dev and links its customer story: https://fly.io/customer-stories/steel-dev/.

employee_band.notes: The company profile reports 56 employees, which falls in the 51-100 band. This is a profile count rather than audited headcount. Source: https://linkedin.com/company/flydotio.

hq_location.notes: hq_city: The company profile explicitly lists Chicago as headquarters. Source: https://linkedin.com/company/fly-io. | hq_country: The company profile identifies Chicago, Illinois, US as headquarters: https://linkedin.com/company/fly-io.

founded_year.notes: Forge explicitly reports 2016: https://forgeglobal.com/flyio_ipo. Other public profiles report 2017, so the founding year remains somewhat uncertain.

eng_blog.notes: Two qualifying infrastructure deep dives are https://fly.io/blog/operationalizing-macaroons and https://fly.io/blog/docker-without-docker/. Both are attributed to Thomas Ptacek; his software-engineering role at Fly.io is documented at https://console.dev/podcast/s02e02-security-thomas-ptacek-fly.io. The posts explain security-token implementation and conversion of container images into Firecracker VMs.

public_docs.notes: The public documentation portal provides guides and references for Machines, Sprites, Managed Postgres, networking and flyctl, rather than a single FAQ. Source: https://docs.fly.io/.

ai_ml_roles_open.notes: The complete jobs index lists Platform Security Engineer, Fullstack Engineer, Infrastructure Operations Engineer, and Networking Engineer: Proxy and Corrosion. None has a qualifying AI, ML or data-science title. Source: https://fly.io/jobs.

model_provider.value: Anthropic and OpenAI (internal inference tooling only)
model_provider.notes: Fly.io names Anthropic and OpenAI for inference in internal tooling. The answer preserves that limitation rather than implying these providers power every customer workload. Source: https://fly.io/legal/security-questionnaire.

compliance_certs.notes: compliance_certs: The security questionnaire claims SOC 2 Type 2 compliance and offers HIPAA support through a BAA for organizations with the paid Compliance Package. HIPAA is conditional BAA coverage, not a blanket application certification. Source: https://fly.io/legal/security-questionnaire. | compliance_certs.0: Fly.io explicitly claims SOC 2 compliance through a Type 2 audit by Aprio: https://fly.io/legal/security-questionnaire. | compliance_certs.1: HIPAA support is offered through a BAA with the paid Compliance Package; this is conditional coverage, not blanket certification of customers' applications. Source: https://fly.io/legal/security-questionnaire.

last_funding.notes: funding_stage: The announcement explicitly calls the $25 million financing Series D. Source: https://fly.io/news/fly-io-launches-computers-for-agents. | funding_date: The funding announcement is dated July 24, 2026, giving the requested month 2026-07. Source: https://fly.io/news/fly-io-launches-computers-for-agents. | funding_amount_usd: The July 2026 announcement states that the Series D round raised $25 million, not cumulative funding. Source: https://fly.io/news/fly-io-launches-computers-for-agents.

raised_18mo.notes: The $25 million Series D announced July 24, 2026 falls within the eighteen months before November 9, 2026. Source: https://fly.io/news/fly-io-launches-computers-for-agents.

hiring_sdr_ae.notes: The complete four-role careers index contains only engineering roles and no SDR, BDR, sales/business development representative or account executive title. Source: https://fly.io/jobs.

launched_6mo.notes: The changelog announces Managed Postgres v2 beta, rebuilt on Fly Machines, on May 19, 2026, and New Fly MCP on October 23, 2026. Both fall within the requested six-month window and are substantive product capabilities. Source: https://fly.io/changelog/.

leadership_change_12mo.notes: On July 24, 2026, Fly.io announced that Scott Johnston had joined as CEO and a board member, within the requested twelve-month window. Source: https://fly.io/news/fly-io-launches-computers-for-agents.

crm_stack_signal.notes: crm_stack_signal: The subprocessor list explicitly identifies HubSpot for customer relationship management and Customer.io for newsletters and transactional email.
